questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Ghana?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Ghana article.

questions.proof: Thirty-one million people live there; its capital was once Cape Coast, but now it is Accra.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Ghana?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Ghana on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Geography” part of the Ghana article.

questions.proof: It is surrounded by Togo to the east, Côte d'Ivoire to the west, Burkina Faso to the north and the Gulf of Guinea (Atlantic Ocean) to the south.

questions.prompt: What money is used in Ghana?

hints.nudge: Money names often come from a country’s own words. The other three are spent in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Ghana article.

questions.proof: 1 Ghana Cedi is equal to 1000 Cedi.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “It is in Western Africa, bordering the Gulf of _____, between Côte d'Ivoire, Nigeria and Togo.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “between”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Ghana article, under the heading “Geography”.

questions.proof: It is surrounded by Togo to the east, Côte d'Ivoire to the west, Burkina Faso to the north and the Gulf of Guinea (Atlantic Ocean) to the south.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “(CI-DI) for their currency but in July _____, “Ghanaian Cedi” became the new currency.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the twenty-first century.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Ghana article.

questions.proof: (CI-DI) for their currency but in July 2007, “Ghanaian Cedi” became the new currency.
